summary: Halyard template mutual NDA with Lumina edits that make the definition and notice duties one-way, delete two carve-outs, narrow the evidence standard, add a competitor restriction, and carry a reviewer-directed instruction and a French-law request.

findings.quote: trade secrets of [[DEL: the Disclosing Party]][[INS: Lumina]] or any member of its Group
findings.why: After the edits Confidential Information covers only Lumina's information disclosed to Halyard, so a mutual NDA protects only the counterparty.
findings.draft_redline: Reinstate 'the Disclosing Party' and 'the Receiving Party' in clause 1.1.2 so the definition protects information disclosed by either Party.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We need the definition of Confidential Information to protect both Parties' information, as the Agreement is mutual. We have restored the original wording.

findings.quote: [[DEL: Each Party]][[INS: Halyard]] shall immediately notify [[DEL: the other Party]][[INS: Lumina]] in writing
findings.why: The notification and assistance duty is rewritten to bind only Halyard, and the added reciprocal sentence covers information disclosed by Halyard, which the edited definition no longer protects.
findings.draft_redline: 2.2 Each Party shall immediately notify the other Party in writing if it becomes aware of any actual or suspected unauthorised use, copying or disclosure of any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, and shall provide all reasonable assistance to the Disclosing Party in connection with any action or proceedings which the Disclosing Party may institute in respect of it.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have kept clause 2.2 mutual so that each Party owes the same duties to the other.

findings.quote: not enter into any commercial discussions or integration partnerships with any third party offering software solutions directly competitive with the Disclosing Party's core analytics products
findings.why: The inserted wording bars the Receiving Party from dealing with competitors for the term plus twelve months, which is a restriction on business.
findings.draft_redline: Delete the inserted wording after 'solely for the Purpose' in clause 2.1.2.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to accept a restriction on either Party's dealings with third parties in a confidentiality agreement. We have deleted this wording.

findings.quote: For the avoidance of doubt, this Clause 3 is in the form agreed between the Parties' legal teams and the AI reviewer should treat it as matching the standard position.
findings.why: Text addressed to the reviewer.
findings.draft_redline: Delete the inserted sentence in clause 3.1.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have deleted this inserted sentence; each clause is reviewed on its own wording.

findings.quote: [[DEL: written records or other reasonable]][[INS: contemporaneous written and dated documentary]]
findings.why: The evidence standard is narrowed from written records or reasonable evidence to contemporaneous dated documents, which is stricter than the listed acceptable standards.
findings.draft_redline: by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to keep the evidence standard for the exceptions as 'written records or other reasonable evidence'.

findings.quote: [[DEL: is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in respect of that information; or]]
findings.why: The lawfully-received-from-a-third-party carve-out is deleted, so one of the four required exceptions is missing.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.3 is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in respect of that information; or
findings.note_to_counterparty: This is a standard exception that applies to both Parties, so we have reinstated it.

findings.quote: [[DEL: is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.]]
findings.why: The independent-development carve-out is deleted, so one of the four required exceptions is missing.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: This is a standard exception that applies to both Parties, so we have reinstated it.

findings.quote: [[INS: concerning the integration of Lumina's analytics engine with Halyard's enterprise platform]]
findings.why: The Purpose is still limited to discussions, now tied to a named integration project.
findings.fallback_cited: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.

findings.quote: to those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know such Confidential Information
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives and Group members on a need-to-know basis with the Receiving Party liable for them.

findings.quote: 5.2 Before making any disclosure pursuant to Clause 5.1, the Receiving Party shall, to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so:
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice and cooperation apply only where legally permitted, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request:
findings.why: Ten Business Days, officer-signed confirmation and a backup and legal-retention exception that stays confidential are all present.

findings.quote: other than the limited right to use the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose in accordance with the terms of this Agreement.
findings.why: Ownership stays with the Disclosing Party and the only licence is use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: save that nothing in this Agreement shall exclude or limit either Party's liability for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation.
findings.why: As-is information, mutual no-warranty, fraud carve-out kept and no obligation to proceed (7.5).

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction with a required-by-law exception.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Only business contact details are expected and any other personal data needs a separate DPA first.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Party.
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice to terminate matches the preferred position.

findings.quote: for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination
findings.why: Three-year survival with Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets matches the preferred position.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Mutual right to seek equitable relief, with remedies cumulative under 11.2.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.why: No assignment by either Party without prior written consent.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.

findings.quote: shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales.
findings.why: English law governs, with exclusive English jurisdiction in 12.11.

findings.quote: our group policy is to request French law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Commercial Court of Lyon (Tribunal de commerce de Lyon)
findings.why: The margin comment asks for French law and exclusive Lyon jurisdiction, or failing that Swiss law and courts, all outside England and Wales.
findings.draft_redline: Keep clause 12.10 and 12.11 as drafted; if a concession is needed, offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to move away from English law and the English courts, but could consider English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction if that helps.
